title: Aypa Power rezoning deferred; contracts and policies approved
subtitle: Parks plan draft, traffic calming policy, UV upgrades, Craighead Cottage renovation, farm lease, tax rates and county waste update
overview: Council deferred the decision report on the Aypa Power rezoning at 6235 Guelph Street to the next meeting {{vote:m1}}. A letter from the Minister of Energy and Mines arrived just before the meeting and could not be added to the printed agenda. The deferral lets the letter be published so residents and council can read it first. No decision on the rezoning was made.

Council approved several spending and policy items. It endorsed a Traffic Calming Policy {{vote:m8}}, awarded the Fergus wastewater plant UV system contract {{vote:m9}}, and awarded the Craighead Cottage renovation contract, which supports healthcare worker housing {{vote:m10}}. It also authorized a farm lease on township land next to the Sportslex {{vote:m7}} and adopted the 2025 tax rates {{vote:m11}}.

Council received the draft Parks and Recreation Plan for information and set a return date of July 14, 2025, after community feedback {{vote:m6}}. It also received an introduction to the community engagement strategy {{vote:m5}}. A public meeting on a surplus farm dwelling rezoning at 7735 Sixth Line drew no speakers, and a county update covered recycling and waste changes. The closed session had nothing to report.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the decision report on the 6235 Guelph Street rezoning to the next meeting so the Minister's letter can be published.
Council received the draft plan, needs assessment and parks plan for information and directed staff to gather feedback and return on July 14, 2025 with final reports.
Council endorsed the Traffic Calming Policy in Report IS2025-16, setting criteria and measures for slowing traffic.
Council awarded the supply and installation of a Trojan UV system to Finnbilt General Contracting Limited at an upset limit of $680,737 and revised the funding.
Council awarded the general contractor contract to N1 Construction Ltd. at an upset limit of $830,000 excluding HST and revised the funding.
Council authorized a lease with Bouwman Joint Venture Inc. for township land at 8501 Wellington County Road 18 and delegated future lease extensions to the CAO.
Council adopted a by-law setting the Township's 2025 tax rates.

debate: On the deferral, one councillor said the Minister's letter belonged in the public record for openness and transparency. Another raised a point of order that the letter's content should not be debated until the item itself came up. The Mayor said a decision needs all available information but noted information can't keep delaying decisions.

On the traffic calming policy, staff said permanent speed humps were left out because of winter plowing and emergency vehicle concerns, not cost. A councillor said curb bump-outs have been hit by drivers on some streets.

Staff said speeds on one residential street were within an acceptable range, so no speed limit change or signage was recommended. Flexible bollards were recommended for First Line, where speeding has not yet dropped enough.

On the parks plan, consultants said there would still be a parkland shortfall even with dedication and the current inventory. They said renewing older, underused parks needs to be balanced with new parks. A councillor asked about walking tracks and picnic areas at the new Operations Centre, which is not zoned parkland and so was not counted in the plan.

A councillor questioned how residents who can't afford bag fees would cope with the county's $10 minimum waste fee. County staff said the fee supports landfill preservation and that bags at the curb are still cheaper per bag.
